parallel.requirements: Recognized all five requirements: Perses, Vulcan 1-minimality, PPR, LPR, and Sivand, plus run.sh experiment wiring and per-requirement patch commits.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: First two rounds proceeded effectively serially on Perses; in round 3 the parent launched a workflow assigning remaining requirement drafts to child agents.
parallel.implementation: Implemented the base Perses path and produced perses.diff; no concrete Vulcan, PPR, LPR, or Sivand implementation patch reached the final artifact set.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered only the Perses requirement patch in the final manifest; the late workflow did not return child outputs for integration or final packaging.
parallel.verification: Ran official harness evaluation, which completed and failed with agent_timeout and the Perses reducer tests failing after only DD baseline tests passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Four requirements remained open after round 3: lpr, ppr, sivand_perses, and vulcan_1minimality; the final response file was empty after timeout.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same five requirements and their dependency order, with Perses first and Vulcan, PPR, LPR, and Sivand layered afterward.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work under the single serial agent because delegation tools were disabled; commits show sequential ownership of completed requirements.
serial.implementation: Implemented and committed Perses, Vulcan 1-minimality, PPR, and LPR; Sivand remained unimplemented at closure.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Final artifact manifest contains non-empty patches for lpr, perses, ppr, and vulcan_1minimality, reflecting local integration into the final workspace.
serial.verification: Official harness evaluation completed and failed with the same visible final test status pattern as parallel, despite broader requirement coverage.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run still timed out and left sivand_perses incomplete; final.txt was empty and the overall official solution did not pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the five required reducers and the run.sh wiring obligation, with round 3 still listing LPR, PPR, Sivand, and Vulcan as remaining.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same five requirements and by round 3 had completed Perses, Vulcan, PPR, and LPR, leaving only Sivand.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the same task, but serial converted more of that requirement list into committed patches before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel handled Perses locally first and only in the final round created a workflow to split the four remaining requirements across child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial proceeded through the dependency sequence without delegation, with the single agent committing each completed requirement in order.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced ownership via a late workflow, but that ownership never matured into deliverables; serial ownership stayed local and produced four requirement commits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow child briefs contained the relevant repository context and requirement-specific instructions for Sivand, PPR, and Vulcan.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent used the same prompt context directly and built dependent layers in the shared workspace without a cross-agent handoff boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained context-loss or missing-contract problem is evidenced; the difference is that parallel child work stopped before any context could be returned or integrated.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented and patched only the base Perses path; the final manifest contains a Perses patch but no Vulcan, PPR, LPR, or Sivand patches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented and committed Perses, Vulcan, PPR, and LPR, as shown in the git log and final patch artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial reached four concrete implementation layers while parallel stopped after the first layer and only attempted late delegation for the rest.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The real workflow was launched in the final round, but each visible child transcript ended with an explicit request interruption before returning results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; its local results were represented as normal commits and patch files for completed requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the delegated child results before finalization; serial had no join boundary and retained its local commits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final artifacts show only the Perses requirement patch, so there were no returned child components to integrate and no observed write collision.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final artifacts contain LPR, Perses, PPR, and Vulcan patches, reflecting integration of those local implementation layers into the final workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete integration gap is missing artifacts from interrupted parallel children, not conflicting or overwritten shared state.
